stick_the_fine_structure_constant.question: The fine-structure constant
references: A. Sommerfeld, Ann. Phys. 356 (1916) 1 (the fine structure of the hydrogen spectrum)
stick_the_fine_structure_constant.statement: Why does the fine-structure constant have the value alpha ~ 1/137.036, and is it truly constant across space and time? No accepted theory derives it from first principles; the open question is its value and its constancy, not its measurement.

ticks.claim: [orbital - speed] The ground-state (n=1) electron's orbital speed is v1 = alpha*c = e^2/(2*eps0*h) = 2.187691e+06 m/s ~ c/137: alpha IS v/c for the innermost orbital.

[orbital - energy] The Rydberg (hydrogen binding/ionization) energy is E_R = 1/2 alpha^2 m_e c^2 = m_e e^4/(8 eps0^2 h^2) = 2.179872e-18 J = 13.6057 eV - the gross-structure scale; it equals h*c*R_inf to 8e-12 (CODATA R_inf), confirming the derivation.

[orbital - size] The Bohr radius is a_0 = hbar/(alpha*m_e*c) = 4*pi*eps0*hbar^2/(m_e e^2) = 5.291772e-11 m, matching CODATA a_0 to 6e-10: alpha sets the atom's size (a_0 = the reduced Compton wavelength / alpha).

[suborbital - fine structure] The suborbital splitting - the spin-orbit and relativistic lifting of the l,j degeneracy within a shell - is suppressed by alpha^2 = 5.325135e-05 relative to the gross structure (fine-structure energy ~ 1/2 alpha^4 m_e c^2 ~ alpha^2 * Rydberg ~ 7.2e-4 eV). This alpha^2-fineness of the spectral lines is why Sommerfeld (1916) named it the FINE-STRUCTURE constant.

[the anchor] alpha is not an abstract number: it is the atom's architecture. The orbital electron's speed (alpha*c), the binding energy (alpha^2), the size (1/alpha in reduced-Compton units), and the fineness of the suborbital splitting (alpha^2) all follow from it - the name is the meaning, the fine structure of the orbitals. Seal the arithmetic; WHY alpha has this value stays the open question.
